questions.q: Which pin marks the AV node?
questions.explain: AV node: floor (inferomedial aspect) of the right atrium, more anterior than the SA node. It passes the impulse to the AV bundle.

questions.q: A newborn takes its first breath. The ductus arteriosus will become which adult structure?
questions.explain: Ductus arteriosus becomes the ligamentum arteriosum, connecting the pulmonary trunk to the aortic arch. The foramen ovale becomes the fossa ovalis.

questions.q: Which pin marks the strip of tissue that gives origin to the pectinate muscles?
questions.explain: Crista terminalis: a strong, tendon-like ridge in the right atrium. The pectinate muscles (comb-like) arise from it.

questions.q: A patient has an infarct that destroys the posteromedial papillary muscle. Which artery supplies it?
questions.explain: Posteromedial papillary muscle: posterior interventricular artery (back of the heart). Anterolateral: anterior interventricular artery (LAD) and circumflex artery.

questions.q: Which pin marks the AV bundle (bundle of His)?
questions.explain: The AV bundle runs along the interventricular septum, then divides into the right and left bundle branches.

questions.q: Which pin marks the pulmonary valve?
questions.explain: Pulmonary valve: a three-cusp semilunar valve at the end of the conus arteriosus. Heard loudest at the left 2nd intercostal space.

questions.q: What is the normal order of conduction through the heart?
options: SA node, bundle branches, AV node, AV bundle, Purkinje fibers
AV node, SA node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
SA node, AV bundle, AV node, Purkinje fibers, bundle branches
SA node, AV node, AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers
questions.explain: The SA node paces, impulses cross internodal pathways to the AV node, then the AV bundle, right and left bundle branches, and Purkinje fibers.

questions.q: Where is the apex beat palpated, and where is the mitral valve best heard?
options: Left 3rd intercostal space at the sternum
questions.explain: The apex points anteriorly, inferiorly and to the left: left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line.

questions.q: What do the papillary muscles and chordae tendineae prevent?
options: Prolapse of the AV valve cusps into the atrium
questions.explain: Papillary muscles contract to hold the AV valve cusps closed. Semilunar valves have no papillary muscles or chordae tendineae.

questions.q: Which pin marks the great cardiac vein?
questions.explain: Great cardiac vein: drains the anterior heart and runs with the anterior interventricular artery (LAD).

questions.q: Which pin marks the diagonal branch?
questions.explain: The diagonal branch crosses the anterior LV. In some people it comes off the circumflex, in others off the anterior interventricular artery.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a branch of the right coronary artery?
questions.explain: The circumflex comes off the left coronary artery. The RCA gives the SA nodal branch, right marginal and posterior interventricular arteries.

questions.q: Why is the left ventricular wall so much thicker than the right?
options: It forms most of the anterior surface
It pumps into the systemic circuit at 100 to 140 mmHg
questions.explain: The LV pumps to the whole body at 100 to 140 mmHg. The RV pumps only through the lungs at 15 to 30 mmHg, so it has a thin wall.

questions.q: Which pin marks the remnant of the foramen ovale?
questions.explain: Fossa ovalis: a depression in the interatrial septum, left behind by the foramen ovale, the fetal shunt that bypassed the lungs.

questions.q: Which pin marks the coronary sinus?
questions.explain: The great, middle and small cardiac veins lead to the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.

questions.q: Which pin marks the ligamentum arteriosum?
questions.explain: Ligamentum arteriosum: remnant of the ductus arteriosus, connecting the pulmonary trunk to the aortic arch. In the newborn it anchors and supports them.

questions.q: The fibrous pericardium is continuous with which structure?
questions.explain: Fibrous pericardium: tough outer layer, attached to the base of the heart and continuous with the central tendon of the diaphragm.

questions.q: Which pin marks the heart's pacemaker?
questions.explain: SA node: the cardiac pacemaker in the superior posterior wall of the right atrium; it sets the heart rate.

questions.q: Which pin marks the right coronary artery?
questions.explain: The RCA runs in the right coronary sulcus between the right auricle and the right ventricle.

questions.q: Which statement about vagal innervation of the heart is correct?
options: The right vagus tends to supply the SA node and the left vagus the AV node
The vagus supplies the ventricular myocardium directly
The left vagus tends to supply the SA node and the right vagus the AV node
questions.explain: Vagal (parasympathetic) fibers supply only the SA and AV nodes and slow the heart: right vagus tends to the SA node, left vagus to the AV node.

questions.q: When does the myocardium receive its coronary blood flow?
questions.explain: The heart can only be fed during diastole, when the ventricles relax. Coronary arteries arise from the base of the ascending aorta.

questions.q: Which pin marks the aortic valve?
questions.explain: Aortic valve: semilunar valve from the left ventricle into the ascending aorta. Heard loudest at the right 2nd intercostal space.

questions.q: Which pin marks the moderator band?
questions.explain: Moderator band (septomarginal trabecula): inferior interventricular septum to the anterior papillary muscle, in the right ventricle only.

questions.q: Sympathetic stimulation of the heart, from spinal cord segments T1 to T5, does what?
questions.explain: Sympathetic fibers go to the nodes and the myocardium: chronotropic (rate) and inotropic (power). The autonomic system does not initiate the beat.

questions.q: A patient has a right coronary artery occlusion. Which complication is most likely?
options: Dysrhythmia from SA or AV node ischemia
questions.explain: The RCA supplies the SA node (about 60%) and the AV node (about 90%), so a right coronary infarct is more likely to cause dysrhythmias.
